subject: Post-call: NovaPay — budget constraints & batching/caching levers
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Zhang <olivia.zhang@novapay.com>, Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@novapay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + quick economics sketch (NovaPay)

Thanks again for a productive call earlier — appreciate you walking us through the production constraints. Below is a quick recap of the problem, goals, and the concrete levers we discussed for lowering inference unit economics. Attaching a short worksheet and our batching/caching cheatsheet for reference.

Key pain points (as you described)
- Monthly inference run-rate ~1.2B tokens across classification and generation flows; heavy tail during billing cycles (5x spike).
- Current vendor costs and token pricing are above internal budget targets — pilot max indicated ~$12k/month.
- Tail latency matters for user-facing flows (goal <300ms p95); some batchable/async flows tolerate 1–2s.
- Security/compliance: need SOC2 evidence and network isolation options during pilot.

Goals we aligned on
- Pilot to demonstrate 30–40% unit-cost reduction and stable p95 latency under typical peak load.
- 6-week technical pilot with production-like traffic sampling (subset of customers).
- Deliverables: cost model, ROI estimate, runbook for rollout, and operational dashboard access.

Levers we recommend (rough TCO implications)
1) Continuous batching for request types that can tolerate small added latency (chatbacks / auxiliary prompts)
   - Expected token/compute reduction: effective throughput improvement 1.35–1.6x depending on request size distribution
2) Prefix / KV caching for repeated context (billing templates, common queries)
   - Can reduce redundant decoding work; conservative savings estimate 8–18% on tokens for high-reuse intents
3) Model sizing + quantization for non-sensitive routes (rerank/summary)
   - Switching to a quantized 8-bit variant for internal-only flows can reduce per-token compute cost by ~30–40% at negligible quality drop for classification/short generation
4) Routing policy: cheaper model fallback for low-risk calls and reserved capacity for high-SLA routes
   - Operationally reduces cost while preserving a high-quality path for critical traffic

Quick sample math (back-of-envelope) — baseline assumptions you shared
- 1.2B tokens/month
- Baseline blended cost per token (current vendor): $0.00045/token -> monthly ~$540k (we know this is above your target)

If pilot achieves combined 35% effective unit-cost reduction via batching + quant + caching:
- New blended cost per token ~= $0.00029 -> monthly ~$348k (net savings on vendor spend ~$192k/month at scale)
- Pilot budget framing: we focus the pilot on confirming a per-token savings curve at your 1.2B/month run-rate; pilot scope will be limited to up to ~5–10% of production traffic to validate assumptions within your $12k pilot cap (we'll simulate scaled economics in the worksheet).

Action items we proposed on the call
- NovaPay: share a 7-day sample of anonymized traffic (headers + token lengths; PII redacted) and a short list of top 10 intents. (Carlos/Olivia)
- Redwood: send a compact SOW + pilot cost table and a prefilled token-econ worksheet for you to review (Rishi + Marissa)
- Security: Redwood will provide SOC2 summary and a checklist of required network settings for Private/VPC pilot (Rishi)

Attachments: token-econ-worksheet.xlsx, redwood-batching-cheatsheet.pdf

If this aligns with your notes, I can follow up with a compact SOW and a proposed 6-week milestone plan.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Olivia Zhang <olivia.zhang@novapay.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@novapay.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + quick economics sketch (NovaPay)

Thanks Rishi — this matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 
- The $12k/month figure is the max our procurement will approve for a pilot without additional approvals. If we can show aggregated savings at the end of pilot, we have room to expand quickly.
- For the sample trace: we can provide a 7-day export with PII redacted by end of next week — Carlos will own that.
- Security: SOC2 is a must; beyond that, we need to confirm encryption-in-transit details and where logs are retained during the pilot.

Please send the SOW and the token-econ worksheet as an editable sheet so our finance team can run the numbers internally. Also include a short section on how Redwood protects customer prompts and KV cache data during the pilot.

- Olivia
Olivia Zhang
Head of ML, NovaPay
olivia.zhang@novapay.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Zhang <olivia.zhang@novapay.com>, Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@novapay.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot scope & milestones (proposal)

Hi Olivia / Carlos — looping in a proposed pilot scope that keeps monthly pilot spend within your stated $12k cap while giving us high-quality signals for scaling economics. High-level proposal: 

Pilot scope (6 weeks)
- Week 0: Kickoff, security checklist, and shared drive with sample logs (NovaPay -> Redwood)
- Weeks 1–3: Staged rollout of up to 5% production traffic routed through Redwood (non-critical intents first)
- Weeks 4–5: Increase to 8–10% for additional traffic patterns; run A/B on routing policies and caching-enabled variants
- Week 6: Readout — dashboard, cost reconciliation, and recommended next steps for expansion

Milestones & success criteria
- Data ingest validated and anonymized by end of Week 0
- Latency p95 for user-facing flows <300ms at 5% traffic; background flows measured separately
- Demonstrable unit-cost delta consistent with 20–40% savings when extrapolated to full run-rate (we'll present confidence intervals)

Material requests from NovaPay
- 7-day anonymized trace (CSV or JSON) with per-request token counts and intent label
- Short list of intents & mapping to SLA class (high/medium/low)

Next steps
- Rishi will send SOW + editable worksheet Monday morning.
- Proposed kickoff (video): Tue 19 May 2027 11:00am PT — does that work for your team?

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Thanks — Tue 19 May 11:00am PT works for us. I've attached the editable token-econ worksheet and a compact SOW draft to the HubSpot record; I'll also drop links in the calendar invite.

Attachments: token-econ-worksheet.xlsx, redwood-batching-cheatsheet.pdf

A few quick notes to close the loop: 
- Security: SOC2 summary and encryption-in-transit details are in the SOW appendix; we'll mail the network configuration checklist after kickoff.
- Pilot spend cap: we will structure test traffic and autoscaling knobs so the experiment fits within the $12k pilot cap you stated; we'll track consumption and alert you if the delta approaches budget so there are no surprises.
- Data sharing: please route the sample export to the shared drive folder we created (link in calendar invite). Once we receive it, Marissa's team will run a 48-hour spike test in a staging slice before live routing.

Looking forward to the kickoff.

Rishi
